GameMetadata

class GameMetadata(id, version, folder_path, entrypoint, view_factory, menu_actions, icon, developers, release_date, required_peripherals, localization, default_language, raw=<factory>)[source]

Bases: object

Game metadata read from metadata.json (schema 1.x).

Attributes:
idstr

Unique game identifier (e.g. "br.udesc.larva.kartea").

versionstr

Game version.

folder_pathPath

Folder where the game is installed.

entrypointstr

File run to start the game, relative to the game folder.

view_factorystr | None

Full path of the game’s view factory class.

menu_actionsdict[str, dict]

Actions the game adds to the platform settings menu.

iconstr | None

Icon path, relative to the game folder.

developerslist[str]

Developer names.

release_datestr | None

Release date (ISO date or just the year).

required_peripheralslist[str]

Required peripherals (e.g. "webcam", "projector").

localizationdict[str, dict[str, str]]

Texts per language code (name, short_description, about_the_game…).

default_languagestr

Language used when the platform language is not available.

rawdict[str, Any]

Full JSON content, for fields not mapped yet. Default is an empty dictionary; it is left out of repr.

SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_MAJORstr, class attribute

Supported major schema version ("1").

FILENAMEstr, class attribute

Metadata file name ("metadata.json").

Methods

load

Read a metadata.json file and return its metadata.

name

Return the display name of the game in a language.

text

Return a text in a language, falling back to the default.
classmethod load(path)[source]

Read a metadata.json file and return its metadata.

Parameters:
pathPath

Path of the metadata.json file; a str is also accepted.

Returns:
GameMetadata

The game metadata; folder_path is the folder of the file.

Raises:
ValueError

If the JSON is invalid, the major schema_version is not SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_MAJOR or a required field is missing.

OSError

If the file cannot be opened.

text(lang, key, default='')[source]

Return a text in a language, falling back to the default.

Parameters:
langstr

Language code, e.g. "pt_BR".

keystr

Text key, e.g. "name".

defaultstr, optional

Value returned when neither language has a non-empty text. Default is "".

Returns:
str

The text in lang, else in default_language, else default.

Examples

>>> loc = {"en_US": {"name": "Game"}}
>>> data = {"id": "g", "version": "1",
...         "runtime": {"entrypoint": "m.py"},
...         "store": {"localization": loc}}
>>> meta = GameMetadata._parse(data, Path("games/g"))
>>> meta.text("pt_BR", "name")
'Game'
>>> meta.name("es_ES")
'Game'
